title: Chapter 4 Review & Practice Test
overview: Bring the whole chapter together: radian measure, exact trig values, equivalent expressions, compound angle formulas and identity proofs. Use the formula sheet and strategy notes, then test yourself on review and practice-test style problems — all written as full-solution questions.
objectives: Convert between degrees and radians and solve arc length and angular velocity problems.
Evaluate trig ratios exactly and with technology.
Use equivalent expressions and compound/double angle formulas to evaluate and simplify.
Solve multi-step applied problems combining the chapter's ideas.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 at a glance
lessons.body:
| Section | Big idea | Key tools |
|---|---|---|
| 4.1 Radian Measure | Angles measured by arc length ÷ radius | $\pi = 180^\circ$, $a = r\theta$, $\omega = \frac{\Delta\theta}{\Delta t}$ |
| 4.2 Trig Ratios and Special Angles | Exact values from the unit circle | special triangles, reference angles, CAST |
| 4.3 Equivalent Expressions | Same values, different forms | cofunction identities, $\pi\pm x$, $\frac{3\pi}{2}\pm x$, $2\pi - x$ |
| 4.4 Compound Angle Formulas | $\sin(x\pm y)$, $\cos(x\pm y)$ | exact values for $\frac{\pi}{12}$-type angles, double angles |
| 4.5 Prove Identities | Show equality for all $x$ | L.S./R.S. method, counterexamples |

**How the ideas connect:** radians (4.1) make the unit circle natural (4.2); symmetry on the unit circle produces equivalent expressions (4.3); the distance formula on the unit circle produces the compound angle formulas (4.4); and all of these are the toolkit for proofs (4.5).

lessons.title: Review strategy
lessons.body:
1. **Rebuild the unit circle from memory** — the special triangles and CAST give every exact value you need.
2. **Classify each question:** convert? evaluate exactly? find an angle? simplify/prove?
3. **Exact means exact:** keep $\pi$ and radicals; round only when asked.
4. **Signs:** before finishing, ask "which quadrant, and is this ratio positive there?"
5. **For proofs:** pick the messier side, convert to sine and cosine, combine fractions, use $\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1$.
6. **Check** numerical answers with a calculator in **radian mode**.

**Common traps to review:** degree mode on the calculator; $\csc x$ vs $\sin^{-1}x$; sign errors in $\cos(x\pm y)$; $\sin(x + y)\ne\sin x + \sin y$; operating on both sides of an identity.

lessons.title: Formula sheet
lessons.body:
**Radians:** $\theta = \frac{a}{r}$, $\pi$ rad $= 180^\circ$, $a = r\theta$, $\omega = \frac{\text{angle}}{\text{time}}$ (1 rev $= 2\pi$ rad).

**Special values**

| | $0$ | $\frac{\pi}{6}$ | $\frac{\pi}{4}$ | $\frac{\pi}{3}$ | $\frac{\pi}{2}$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sin | 0 | $\frac12$ | $\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ | $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ | 1 |
| cos | 1 | $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ | $\frac12$ | 0 |
| tan | 0 | $\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$ | 1 | $\sqrt3$ | undefined |

**Equivalent expressions:** $\sin x = \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)$, $\cos x = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)$, $\sin(\pi - x) = \sin x$, $\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x$, $\sin(\pi + x) = -\sin x$, $\cos(2\pi - x) = \cos x$.

**Compound angles:** $\sin(x\pm y) = \sin x\cos y\pm\cos x\sin y$, $\cos(x\pm y) = \cos x\cos y\mp\sin x\sin y$.

**Double angles:** $\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x$, $\cos 2x = \cos^2x - \sin^2x = 1 - 2\sin^2x = 2\cos^2x - 1$.

**Pythagorean:** $\sin^2x + \cos^2x = 1$, $1 + \tan^2x = \sec^2x$, $1 + \cot^2x = \csc^2x$.

lessons.title: Chapter problem: transportation engineering
lessons.body:
Many chapter questions used transportation contexts. Two summary problems:

**Bypass road.** A highway runs east 2 km, then turns southward through $\frac{\pi}{12}$ and runs another 2 km. An arc-shaped bypass is centred at the bend with radius 2 km, joining the two ends. The two highway segments are radii of the arc, and the angle between them is $\pi - \frac{\pi}{12} = \frac{11\pi}{12}$, so the bypass length is $a = r\theta = 2\times\frac{11\pi}{12} = \frac{11\pi}{6}\approx 5.76$ km.

**Suspension bridge.** A 50 m tower has two cables on each side, at inclinations $x$ and $2x$. Their total length is
$$l = \frac{50}{\sin x} + \frac{50}{\sin 2x} = \frac{50(2\cos x)}{\sin 2x} + \frac{50}{\sin 2x} = \frac{50(1 + 2\cos x)}{\sin 2x}.$$

realWorld.title: Careers
realWorld.body: Computer hardware engineers, game developers, surveyors and aerospace engineers use radian measure and identities every day.

realWorld.title: Transportation
realWorld.body: On-ramps, bypasses and bank angles of aircraft are all designed using arc length and trig identities.

realWorld.title: Astronomy
realWorld.body: The Moon orbits Earth every 27.3 days: its angular velocity is $\frac{2\pi}{27.3}\approx 0.230$ rad/day, so it moves about $384\,400\times 0.230\approx 88\,500$ km along its orbit each day.

practice.question: Determine the exact radian measure of $105^\circ$ and the exact degree measure of $\frac{13\pi}{24}$.
Which expression is equivalent to $\sin x$: $\cos\left(x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ or $\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + x\right)$? Explain.
practice.solution: $\cos\left(x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \cos x\cdot 0 + \sin x\cdot 1 = \sin x$; the other equals $-\sin x$.

practice.question: A runner runs 60 m along a circular track of radius 20 m. What is the sector angle?

summary: Radians: $\theta = \frac{a}{r}$, $\pi$ rad = 180°, arc length $a = r\theta$, angular velocity in rad/s.
Exact values of special angles and their multiples come from the unit circle, special triangles and CAST.
Equivalent expressions and cofunction identities relate $f(x)$ to functions of $\frac{\pi}{2}\pm x$, $\pi\pm x$, etc.
Compound and double angle formulas give exact values and simplify expressions.
Identities are proved by transforming each side independently; one counterexample disproves.

questions.text: Convert as indicated.
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) ${{d}}^\circ\times\frac{\pi}{180}\approx {{d*pi/180:3}}$ rad.

(b) ${{r}}\times\frac{180^\circ}{\pi}\approx {{r*180/pi:4}}^\circ$.

(c) ${{15*n}}^\circ = \frac{ {{15*n}}\pi}{180} = \frac{ {{n}}\pi}{12}$.

(d) $\frac{ {{m}}\pi}{18} = {{m}}\times 10^\circ = {{10*m}}^\circ$.

questions.text: Turntables for vinyl records have speeds of 16, 33⅓, 45 and 78 rpm. A microwave turntable turns {{t}} times per minute.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Summarise the angular velocity of each record speed in °/s and rad/s in a table.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the microwave turntable's angular velocity in rad/s.

questions.modelAnswer:
Use $\omega(°/s) = \text{rpm}\times 6$ and $\omega(\text{rad/s}) = \text{rpm}\times\frac{2\pi}{60} = \frac{\text{rpm}\cdot\pi}{30}$.

| rpm | °/s | rad/s |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 96 | $\frac{8\pi}{15}\approx 1.68$ |
| 33⅓ | 200 | $\frac{10\pi}{9}\approx 3.49$ |
| 45 | 270 | $\frac{3\pi}{2}\approx 4.71$ |
| 78 | 468 | $\frac{13\pi}{5}\approx 8.17$ |

Microwave: ${{t*6}}^\circ$/s and $\frac{ {{t}}\pi}{30}\approx {{t*pi/30:3}}$ rad/s.

rubric.point: Correct method converting rpm to rad/s

questions.text: The Moon orbits Earth once every 27.3 days at an orbital radius of about {{R}} km.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Determine the angular velocity of the Moon in degrees per day and radians per day.

parts.label: b
parts.text: How far does the Moon travel along its orbit each day?

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $\omega = \frac{360^\circ}{27.3}\approx 13.2^\circ$/day $= \frac{2\pi}{27.3}\approx 0.230$ rad/day.

(b) $a = r\theta = {{R}}\times\frac{2\pi}{27.3}\approx {{R*2*pi/27.3:3}}$ km per day.

rubric.point: Angular velocity in degrees per day
Angular velocity in radians per day

questions.text: A gymnasium has a circular running track of radius {{r}} m. A runner runs {{a}} m along the track.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Determine the sector angle in radians.

questions.modelAnswer: $\theta = \frac{a}{r} = \frac{ {{a}} }{ {{r}} }\approx {{a/r:3}}$ rad $\approx {{a/r*180/pi:3}}^\circ$.

questions.text: Use a calculator to determine the six trigonometric ratios of $\frac{ {{n}}\pi}{ {{k}} }$, to four decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
Radian mode: $\theta = \frac{ {{n}}\pi}{ {{k}} }\approx {{n*pi/k:4}}$.

$\sin\theta\approx {{sin(n*pi/k):4}}$, $\cos\theta\approx {{cos(n*pi/k):4}}$, $\tan\theta\approx {{tan(n*pi/k):4}}$, $\csc\theta\approx {{1/sin(n*pi/k):4}}$, $\sec\theta\approx {{1/cos(n*pi/k):4}}$, $\cot\theta\approx {{1/tan(n*pi/k):4}}$.

questions.text:
Determine an exact value for each expression.

(a) $\cot\frac{\pi}{4}\cos\frac{\pi}{6}\csc\frac{\pi}{3}$

(b) $\cos\frac{\pi}{3}\csc\frac{\pi}{6} - \sin\frac{\pi}{2}$

(c) $\dfrac{\sin\frac{\pi}{6} + \cos\frac{5\pi}{3}}{1 + \tan\frac{3\pi}{4}\cot\frac{\pi}{4}}$ (if the expression is undefined, explain why)
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $1\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt3} = 1$.

(b) $\frac12\cdot 2 - 1 = 0$.

(c) Numerator $= \frac12 + \frac12 = 1$; denominator $= 1 + (-1)(1) = 0$. Division by zero: the expression is **undefined**.

questions.text: Two guy wires are attached to the top of a radio antenna {{h}} m high. They make angles of $\frac{\pi}{3}$ and $\frac{\pi}{4}$ with the ground, on opposite sides of the antenna.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Determine an exact expression for the distance between the two anchor points A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Evaluate it to the nearest tenth.

parts.label: c
parts.text: What would the distance be if both wires were on the same side of the antenna?

questions.modelAnswer:
Horizontal distance from the base to each anchor: $d = \frac{h}{\tan\theta}$.

$d_1 = \frac{ {{h}} }{\tan\frac{\pi}{3}} = \frac{ {{h}} }{\sqrt3}$, $d_2 = \frac{ {{h}} }{\tan\frac{\pi}{4}} = {{h}}$.

(a) $AB = {{h}} + \frac{ {{h}} }{\sqrt3} = {{h}}\left(1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt3}\right)$ m.

(b) $\approx {{h*(1+1/sqrt(3)):4}}$ m.

(c) If both wires were on the same side, $AB = {{h}} - \frac{ {{h}} }{\sqrt3}\approx {{h*(1-1/sqrt(3)):3}}$ m.

questions.text: (a) Given $\cot\frac{2\pi}{5} = \tan z$, express $\frac{2\pi}{5}$ as a difference between $\frac{\pi}{2}$ and an angle, and apply a cofunction identity to find $z$. (b) Given $\cos\frac{5\pi}{8} = -\sin y$, express $\frac{5\pi}{8}$ as a sum of $\frac{\pi}{2}$ and an angle and find $y$.
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $\frac{2\pi}{5} = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{10}$. $\cot\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right) = \tan x$, so $z = \frac{\pi}{10}$.

(b) $\frac{5\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{2} + \frac{\pi}{8}$. $\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + x\right) = -\sin x$, so $y = \frac{\pi}{8}$.

questions.text: Given that $\tan\frac{4\pi}{9}\approx 5.6713$, determine, to four decimal places and without a calculator, (a) $\cot\frac{\pi}{18}$ and (b) $\tan\frac{13\pi}{9}$. Justify each answer. (c) Given $\cos\frac{7\pi}{15}\approx 0.1045$, determine $\sin\frac{29\pi}{30}$.
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $\frac{\pi}{18} = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{4\pi}{9}$: $\cot\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right) = \tan x$, so $5.6713$.

(b) $\frac{13\pi}{9} = \pi + \frac{4\pi}{9}$: $\tan(\pi + x) = \tan x$, so $5.6713$.

(c) $\frac{29\pi}{30} = \frac{\pi}{2} + \frac{7\pi}{15}$: $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + x\right) = \cos x$, so $0.1045$.

questions.text: Given $\sin x = \cos\frac{3\pi}{11}$ and that $x$ lies in the second quadrant, determine $x$ exactly. Also determine an exact acute angle $y$ such that $\sin y = \cos {{m}}y$.
questions.modelAnswer:
$\cos\frac{3\pi}{11} = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{3\pi}{11}\right) = \sin\frac{5\pi}{22}$. In QII, $x = \pi - \frac{5\pi}{22} = \frac{17\pi}{22}$.

$\sin y = \cos {{m}}y = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - {{m}}y\right)$, so $y + {{m}}y = \frac{\pi}{2}$ and $y = \frac{\pi}{ {{2*(m+1)}} }\approx {{pi/(2*(m+1)):4}}$.

questions.text:
Use an appropriate compound angle formula to express each as a single trigonometric function, and then determine an exact value.

(a) $\sin\frac{5\pi}{12}\cos\frac{\pi}{4} - \cos\frac{5\pi}{12}\sin\frac{\pi}{4}$

(b) $\sin\frac{5\pi}{12}\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + \cos\frac{5\pi}{12}\sin\frac{\pi}{4}$

(c) $\cos\frac{5\pi}{12}\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + \sin\frac{5\pi}{12}\sin\frac{\pi}{4}$

(d) $\cos\frac{5\pi}{12}\cos\frac{\pi}{4} - \sin\frac{5\pi}{12}\sin\frac{\pi}{4}$
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{12} - \frac{3\pi}{12}\right) = \sin\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac12$.

(b) $\sin\frac{8\pi}{12} = \sin\frac{2\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

(c) $\cos\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

(d) $\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\frac12$.

questions.text: Angles $x$ and $y$ are in the first quadrant with $\sin x = \frac{ {{A1}} }{ {{C1}} }$ and $\cos y = \frac{ {{A2}} }{ {{C2}} }$.
Angle $a$ is in the second quadrant with $\sin a = \frac{12}{13}$. Angle $b$ is in the third quadrant with $\cos b = -\frac35$. Determine exact values of $\sin(a + b)$ and $\cos(a - b)$.
questions.modelAnswer:
$\cos a = -\frac{5}{13}$, $\sin b = -\frac45$.

$\sin(a + b) = \frac{12}{13}\left(-\frac35\right) + \left(-\frac{5}{13}\right)\left(-\frac45\right) = \frac{-36 + 20}{65} = -\frac{16}{65}$.

$\cos(a - b) = \left(-\frac{5}{13}\right)\left(-\frac35\right) + \frac{12}{13}\left(-\frac45\right) = \frac{15 - 48}{65} = -\frac{33}{65}$.

rubric.point: cos a and sin b with correct signs

questions.text: Angle $x$ lies in the third quadrant and $\tan x = \frac{7}{24}$. Determine exact values for $\cos 2x$ and $\sin 2x$. Use your answers to decide in which quadrant the terminal arm of $2x$ lies.
questions.modelAnswer:
Reference triangle 7-24-25; in QIII $\sin x = -\frac{7}{25}$, $\cos x = -\frac{24}{25}$.

$\cos 2x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x = \frac{576 - 49}{625} = \frac{527}{625}$.

$\sin 2x = 2\left(-\frac{7}{25}\right)\left(-\frac{24}{25}\right) = \frac{336}{625}$.

Both positive, so $2x$ has its terminal arm in quadrant I (here $2\pi < 2x < 3\pi$ wraps around to QI).

rubric.point: Correct sin x and cos x with signs

questions.text: Determine an exact value for $\cos\frac{13\pi}{12}$ in two different ways, and show that they agree.
questions.modelAnswer:
Method 1: $\frac{13\pi}{12} = \pi + \frac{\pi}{12}$ so $\cos\frac{13\pi}{12} = -\cos\frac{\pi}{12} = -\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - \frac{\pi}{4}\right) = -\left(\frac12\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt2} + \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\right) = -\frac{1 + \sqrt3}{2\sqrt2}$.

Method 2: $\frac{13\pi}{12} = \frac{3\pi}{4} + \frac{\pi}{3}$: $\cos\frac{3\pi}{4}\cos\frac{\pi}{3} - \sin\frac{3\pi}{4}\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = -\frac{1}{2\sqrt2} - \frac{\sqrt3}{2\sqrt2} = -\frac{1 + \sqrt3}{2\sqrt2}$.

Both $\approx -0.9659$ ✓

questions.text: Prove that $\sin(2\pi - x) = -\sin x$.
questions.modelAnswer: L.S. $= \sin 2\pi\cos x - \cos 2\pi\sin x = 0 - \sin x = -\sin x =$ R.S. ∎

questions.text: Prove that $2\sin x\cos y = \sin(x + y) + \sin(x - y)$.
questions.modelAnswer: R.S. $= (\sin x\cos y + \cos x\sin y) + (\sin x\cos y - \cos x\sin y) = 2\sin x\cos y =$ L.S. ∎

questions.text: Prove that $(\sin 2x)(\tan x + \cot x) = 2$.
questions.modelAnswer: L.S. $= 2\sin x\cos x\cdot\frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x\cos x} = 2 =$ R.S. ∎

questions.text: Prove that $\dfrac{\sin 2x}{\sec x} = \dfrac{2\cos^2 x}{\csc x}$.
questions.modelAnswer: L.S. $= 2\sin x\cos x\cdot\cos x = 2\sin x\cos^2 x$. R.S. $= 2\cos^2 x\cdot\sin x = 2\sin x\cos^2 x$. L.S. = R.S. ∎

questions.text: Prove that $\dfrac{\sin(x + y)}{\cos x\cos y} = \tan x + \tan y$.
questions.modelAnswer: L.S. $= \frac{\sin x\cos y + \cos x\sin y}{\cos x\cos y} = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \frac{\sin y}{\cos y} = \tan x + \tan y =$ R.S. ∎

questions.text: Consider the equation $\cos 2x = 2\sin x\sec x$. Either prove that it is an identity or determine a counterexample. Then explain how you could have predicted the result from the graphs of the two sides.
questions.modelAnswer:
R.S. $= \frac{2\sin x}{\cos x} = 2\tan x$, which is not $\cos 2x$. Counterexample $x = \frac{\pi}{4}$: L.S. $= \cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0$, R.S. $= 2\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 2$. Not an identity.

The graph of $2\tan x$ has vertical asymptotes and an unbounded range, while $\cos 2x$ stays between −1 and 1, so the graphs clearly differ.

questions.text: (a) Describe how graphing technology could be used to decide whether it is reasonable to conjecture that $\cos 3x = \cos^3 x - 3\cos x\sin^2 x$. (b) Develop a formula for $\cos 3x$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$ to prove the conjecture. (c) Check at $x = {{x}}$.
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) Graph $Y_1 = \cos 3x$ and $Y_2 = \cos^3 x - 3\cos x\sin^2 x$ in radian mode; if the curves coincide, the conjecture is reasonable.

(b) $\cos 3x = \cos(2x + x) = \cos 2x\cos x - \sin 2x\sin x = (\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x)\cos x - 2\sin x\cos x\sin x = \cos^3 x - \cos x\sin^2 x - 2\cos x\sin^2 x = \cos^3 x - 3\cos x\sin^2 x$ ∎

(c) $\cos({{3*x}})\approx {{cos(3*x):4}}$ and $\cos^3 {{x}} - 3\cos {{x}}\sin^2 {{x}}\approx {{cos(x)^3 - 3*cos(x)*sin(x)^2:4}}$ ✓

questions.text: A highway enters a city and runs east for {{d}} km. It then turns southward through an angle of $\frac{\pi}{12}$ and runs another {{d}} km before leaving the city. Engineers design an arc-shaped bypass with its centre at the bend and radius {{d}} km, joining the point where the highway enters the city to the point where it leaves.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe a sketch of the old highway and the bypass and find the central angle of the bypass arc.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Determine the length of the bypass to the nearest hundredth of a kilometre.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Compare the length of the bypass with the route through the city.

questions.modelAnswer:
(i) The two straight segments are radii of the bypass circle (both {{d}} km from the bend). The highway turns through $\frac{\pi}{12}$, so the angle between the two segments at the bend is $\pi - \frac{\pi}{12} = \frac{11\pi}{12}$.

(ii) Bypass length $a = r\theta = {{d}}\times\frac{11\pi}{12}\approx {{d*11*pi/12:3}}$ km.

(iii) The highway route through the city is $2\times{{d}} = {{2*d}}$ km, and bypass − highway $\approx {{d*11*pi/12 - 2*d:3}}$ km.

rubric.point: Describes or sketches the diagram with radii and angle
Finds the central angle 11π/12 with reasoning

questions.text: An A-frame ski chalet has a front face formed by two sloping sides. Its extension shed is attached so that the total height is made up of a 5 m length rising at angle $c$ and a 5 m length rising at angle $2c$ (measured from the horizontal).
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $h = 5\sin c + 5\sin 2c = 5\sin c + 5(2\sin c\cos c) = 5\sin c(1 + 2\cos c)$.

(b) With $c = \frac{\pi}{ {{k}} }$: $h = 5\sin\frac{\pi}{ {{k}} }\left(1 + 2\cos\frac{\pi}{ {{k}} }\right)\approx {{5*sin(pi/k)*(1+2*cos(pi/k)):4}}$ m.

rubric.point: Expresses h as sum of vertical components

questions.text: Several Practice Test items ask you to pick an expression equivalent to $\sin x$. Without a list of options, write **three** different expressions equivalent to $\sin x$ that use cosine or a shifted sine, and **two** expressions that look similar but are *not* equivalent. Justify each one.
questions.modelAnswer:
Equivalent: $\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)$ (cofunction); $\cos\left(x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ (cosine is even, same as previous); $\sin(\pi - x)$ (reflection in the $y$-axis); $-\cos\left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

Not equivalent: $\cos\left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -\sin x$; $\sin(\pi + x) = -\sin x$; $\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x$. Each can be justified by expanding with a compound angle formula, e.g. $\cos\left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \cos x\cdot 0 - \sin x\cdot 1 = -\sin x$.

rubric.point: Valid justification (compound angle or unit circle)

questions.text:
Correct and justify each statement (each one is false as written):

(a) "$\frac{13\pi}{24}$ rad is less than a right angle."

(b) "$\sin\frac{15\pi}{17}$ is negative because $\frac{15\pi}{17}$ is close to $\pi$."

(c) "If $\cot\theta = -1$ and $\theta$ is in quadrant II, then $\sec\theta = \sqrt2$."
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $\frac{13\pi}{24} = 97.5^\circ$, which is **greater** than a right angle ($\frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{12\pi}{24}$).

(b) $\frac{15\pi}{17}$ is less than $\pi$, so it is in quadrant II where sine is **positive**: $\sin\frac{15\pi}{17}\approx 0.3612$.

(c) $\theta = \frac{3\pi}{4}$; $\cos\theta = -\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$, so $\sec\theta = -\sqrt2$ (negative in QII).
